Hi Miguel / TitanCloud team,

Attaching an initial cut of the private VPC gateway proposal we discussed on the call last week. The two artifacts are attached: a concise topology diagram (vpc-gateway-scaling-v1.pdf) and a sequence snapshot of the control-plane / data-plane interaction (data-path-sequence.drawio.png).

Key asks:
- Can you verify the proposed gateway sizing and the failover model for active/passive vs active/active?
- Any constraints on connection churn from your side (BGP flaps, session limits)?
- Review the control-plane coupling points noted on page 3 — we want to avoid a common state-store dependency in the gateway path.

Notes for the Redwood team (cc'd): please pay attention to egress NAT translation limits and the tracing headers we plan to inject. I sketched a draft runbook for the handover (runbook-gateway-egress-draft.docx) — expect that to change.

Subject: Re: Private VPC gateway scaling & data-path review

Laura — thanks for the clear artifacts. Quick initial comments after a quick pass:

1) Active/Active preferred: from a TitanCloud ops perspective, active/active with per-connection hashing gives better utilization across racks. If you stick to active/passive you'll need higher headroom per site.
2) Session caps: our gateway nodes have a soft limit at ~350k concurrent TCP sessions per instance (default config). If you expect bursty north-south traffic, plan for session pooling or connection proxying.
3) Control-plane coupling: agree that embedding a centralized state store in the fast path is risky. Suggested alternate: a compact pre-warmed KV cache per gateway backed by async sync from control-plane; this keeps the fast path local.
4) NAT behavior: ensure consistent 5-tuple hashing at the egress NAT so return path pinning is stable across gateway failovers.

I'll run the diagram with our infra team today and get back with specific instance types and a recommended autoscale curve. Also flagging that ACME (if they're in the loop) has a weird BGP hold-time they wanted to call out — cc them if you want their input.

—Miguel

Thanks Miguel — this is helpful. A few operational items I want to capture so we can add them to NETOPS-1245:

- Action: add an async per-gateway KV with TTL for auth_tokens and route hints; control-plane emits deltas, gateways apply idempotently. (Owner: Jonas)
- Action: run a connection churn test at the TitanCloud staging cluster to validate the 350k session cap hypothesis. (Owner: TitanCloud)
- Action: confirm that our eBPF-based load balancer preserves the 5-tuple for NAT hashing. If not, add a connection pinning layer. (Owner: Aditya)

I'm attaching a short checklist in the Google Drive link (see related_links) — I'll convert the checklist into a short runbook section once Miguel confirms instance sizing.

Good sanity check for our autoscale windows.

A couple compliance/security notes we need on the diagrams and runbook before we hand this to customers: 

- Egress logging: ensure all egress interfaces can stream to our secure logging endpoint with TLS 1.3 and that keys are rotated via KMS. Put a toggle in the runbook for sampling vs full capture.
- Flow-level masking: any PII in headers must be scrubbed before it hits persistent logs — add the scrub rule example to the runbook.
- Audit evidence: capture the control-plane rollout timestamps and route artifacts (attach as JSON snapshot) so we can satisfy SOC2 evidence requests.

If TitanCloud is doing active/active, we need to ensure each gateway exposes health and readiness endpoints compatible with our canary tooling. Miguel — can you confirm the endpoints and path?

Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
